response.original_title: Must We Say What We Mean
response.overview: From website: "‘Must We Say What We Mean?’ is a work of meta-criticism, made over the course of more than three years, that explores an apparently simple assumption: an act of film criticism, whether written or videographic, should seek both an understanding of one’s object, and the understanding of one’s audience. Taking the wordless ending of Before Sunrise (Richard Linklater, 1995) as our object, we pursue the implications of this assumption in various forms - from a range of creative experiments with the film, to a series of recorded video calls between the authors. Our video essay is a distillation of this material, and we finally offer illustrated recorded critical conversations as one valuable, medium-specific mode of videographic film criticism."
response.title: Must We Say What We Mean
